content.text: Ling Guang, I just received a health alert for Cybercat. The neural signal reception rate has dropped significantly, and the activity heatmap shows abnormal avoidance behavior. I'm a bit worried—this is the first malfunction since its chip was implanted.
Optimus Prime, don't rush. First, tell me the chip model and implantation time, and whether there have been any recent software updates. I need this basic data to analyze.

The chip is NeuroSync Pro, implanted for almost a year. The software was automatically updated to the latest version last month, but it had been running stably before. I suspect it might be due to environmental interference.
The stability of NeuroSync Pro is generally good, but signal interference or chip aging can be potential issues. Have you made any recent changes to your home network or smart devices?
Yes, I upgraded my smart home system last week and introduced a new wireless protocol. Here is the network structure diagram, which might be relevant.

This is most likely the source of interference. The new protocol may conflict with the communication frequency band of the chip. Let's conduct an environmental variable control test: turn off some smart devices and observe the signal changes.
Good idea. I'll go turn off the smart lighting and audio system in the living room, then start monitoring again. What data should be recorded?

Record the changes in neural signal reception rate and activity heat map every half hour. Also, monitor whether the cat's behavior returns to normal. This will help us locate the source of interference.
Understood. I'll start the test now and give you feedback in half an hour. Hopefully, it's just temporary interference—I really don't want to see Cyber Cat having issues.
Stay calm, Optimus Prime. Technical glitches are common, and we have a systematic approach to troubleshoot. Remember to record detailed data, as it is crucial for subsequent analysis.
Half an hour has passed, and the signal reception rate has slightly recovered, but the activity heatmap still shows anomalies. Here is the latest monitoring screenshot.

The signal recovery is a good sign, indicating that the interference may have come from the device that was turned off. However, the abnormal behavior persists, suggesting there might be an issue with the chip itself or the software. Have you checked the physical connections of the chip?
The physical connection appears normal with no signs of looseness. Could it be that a software update introduced a bug? I recall that after the last update, the cat's response was a bit delayed.
Possibly. Software bugs can cause abnormal signal processing. It is recommended that you roll back to the previous stable version while continuing environmental testing to rule out multiple factors.
Okay, I'll try rolling back the software. Additionally, I noticed that the cat avoids the smart home control center area, and the heat map shows the signal is weakest there.

This further points to environmental interference. The control center may be a strong signal source. Continue shutting down more devices, such as smart thermostats and security systems, to see if the signal improves.

Software rollback completed, signal reception rate has significantly improved and is approaching normal levels. However, the activity heatmap still shows slight anomalies, and the cat appears to be adjusting.

Great, software issues have been largely ruled out. Now, focus on environmental interference: gradually restart the smart devices, monitor signal changes, and identify the specific source of interference.
I'll proceed according to your plan and record the data. This malfunction has made me more aware of the fragility of technological aesthetics, but your systematic thinking has been a great help.
Technological ethics require us to handle enhancement systems with caution. Optimus Prime, by cooperating with the tests and maintaining continuous records, we can certainly resolve this issue.
